title: Close the login email timing side channel

claims.statement: Claude Code (claude-code) is the source-producing agent for CHG-0075 under human principal @rodrigoteamx, on the 2026-08-24 directive 'dale al merge y a lo que sigue' — the ninth hardening fix, closing the login email timing side channel. This does not authorize automatic merge of CHG-0075.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md, profile.json actors and the 2026-08-24 user directive.

claims.statement: The hardening audit found AuthService.login runs the scrypt derivation only when the submitted email matches the owner: the boolean short-circuit skips verifyPassword on a non-matching email, so a matching-email attempt (the derivation runs) is measurably slower than a non-matching one, revealing the owner's email by timing.
claims.evidence: server/src/auth/AuthService.ts login prior short-circuit; the 2026-08-24 hardening-audit finding hardening-login-email-timing.

claims.statement: The change always runs a password derivation — against a fixed decoy verifier that carries the real scrypt parameters when there is no owner or the email differs — then rejects with INVALID_CREDENTIALS unless the email matched and the password verified.
claims.evidence: server/src/auth/AuthService.ts DECOY_PASSWORD_VERIFIER and the rewritten login.

claims.statement: Governed discovery equalized the derivation, which dominates login cost, so a non-matching email now performs the same scrypt work as a matching one; the decoy reuses the real cost, block size, parallelization and key length so the two paths are equivalent.
claims.evidence: server/src/auth/AuthService.ts DECOY_PASSWORD_VERIFIER uses SCRYPT_COST, SCRYPT_BLOCK_SIZE, SCRYPT_PARALLELIZATION and SCRYPT_KEY_LENGTH.

claims.statement: Proving via a derivation hook that a scrypt derivation runs exactly once for a non-matching email, a matching email with the wrong password, and correct credentials, closes the login email timing side channel.

The decoy uses the real scrypt parameters; the empty-password early return in verifyPassword still skips the derivation, but that reflects the caller's own empty input rather than the owner's email, so it is not an email oracle.
claims.evidence: server/src/auth/AuthService.ts verifyPassword returns false for an empty password before deriving.

claims.statement: The change is server-only and additive: the login derivation path, a fixed decoy verifier, an optional test hook, and a test. No protocol or Studio change, and login behavior is unchanged for valid and invalid credentials.
claims.evidence: git diff of the CHG-0075 branch: server/src/auth/AuthService.ts and server/tests/unit/loginTiming.test.ts.

successCriteria.statement: A password derivation runs for a non-matching email, not only a matching one.
successCriteria.verification: A test with a derivation hook asserts a derivation runs exactly once when logging in with an email that is not the owner's.

successCriteria.statement: A derivation runs on the matching-email and correct-credentials paths too, and behavior is unchanged.
successCriteria.verification: The test asserts a derivation runs once for a matching email with a wrong password (rejects) and once for correct credentials (issues a session).
The full server suite passes and the server type-check passes.

definitionOfDone.statement: CHG-0075 records the login timing finding and its constant-derivation fix before implementation.
definitionOfDone.evidence: Schema-valid record and deterministic governance compilation.

definitionOfDone.statement: login always runs a scrypt derivation, against a fixed decoy verifier when there is no owner or the email differs.
A test proves the derivation runs on the non-matching, wrong-password and correct paths; the full server suite passes.
Governance, licensing, lint, type-check, focused and full tests, build, dependency audit and diff checks pass before handoff.
definitionOfDone.evidence: npm run governance:check, npm run check, npm run build, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities), ESLint, type-check and git diff --check; the accept commit is verified by its own pull-request Constitution run before merge.
